questions.stem: A downstream GTP-U node rejects inner fragments after an IPsec tunnel. Which change delivers a complete inner datagram?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Set ip-fragmentation post-encapsulation on both sending peers
choices.feedback: Correct: the receiver reassembles outer ESP fragments before decrypting, so the clear side receives the complete GTP-U packet.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Increase the downstream host's UDP receive buffer first
choices.feedback: A larger socket buffer does not change where FortiGate fragments the inner packet; the downstream node still receives fragments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Enable NAT traversal and lower the ESP replay window
choices.feedback: NAT traversal changes ESP transport encapsulation and ports, not the pre/post fragmentation point.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable NPU offload and leave pre-encapsulation enabled
choices.feedback: Disabling offload may change processing cost, but pre-encapsulation still forwards inner fragments to the downstream node.

questions.stem: Throughput falls after switching to post-encapsulation fragmentation. Which evidence best isolates receiver-side pressure?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase tunnel MTU and ignore fragment counters
choices.feedback: Increasing MTU may reduce fragmentation, but it does not identify HPE rate limiting or reassembly-memory exhaustion.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inspect HPE_IPSEC_ESP, HPE_IP_FRAG and ReasmFails
choices.feedback: Correct: HPE counters expose CPU protection drops, while ReasmFails indicates fragment reassembly trouble.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Disable DLP inspection on the downstream policy
choices.feedback: DLP inspection is unrelated to outer ESP fragment reassembly and would not explain these counters.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Lower the IPsec replay window to accept fragments
choices.feedback: Replay-window changes do not fix CPU rate limits or exhausted reassembly buffers.

questions.stem: Two FortiGates carry oversized traffic in both directions. Where must the fragmentation mode be configured?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Only on the receiver that decrypts traffic
choices.feedback: The receiver does not choose how the remote peer fragments before encryption; the encrypting side makes that decision.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only on the hub that owns the tunnel
choices.feedback: A hub-only setting leaves the opposite direction using the other peer's configured mode.

choices.label: C
choices.text: On each peer when that peer encrypts traffic
choices.feedback: Correct: fragmentation is applied by the encrypting side, so configure each sender for its outbound direction.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The mode is negotiated once during IKE establishment
choices.feedback: The setting is not negotiated as a single IKE parameter that automatically overrides both configurations.

questions.stem: A GTP-U packet exceeds the tunnel interface MTU before encryption. What happens even with post-encapsulation selected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The receiver reassembles it before any encryption
choices.feedback: Reassembly at the receiver cannot occur before the sender has encrypted and transmitted the packet.

choices.label: B
choices.text: ESP bypasses the interface MTU after encryption
choices.feedback: ESP overhead can exceed the underlay MTU; it does not bypass the tunnel interface's inner MTU.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only TCP MSS adjustment controls GTP-U size
choices.feedback: MSS adjustment applies to TCP and does not control UDP GTP-U datagrams.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The oversized inner packet fragments before IPsec processing
choices.feedback: Correct: packets larger than the tunnel interface MTU are fragmented before IPsec processing regardless of the post-encapsulation setting.

questions.stem: A package has a clock icon beside its name. What does that prove?

choices.label: A
choices.text: A recurring schedule is attached to that policy package
choices.feedback: Correct: the clock indicator identifies an attached schedule; it proves intent, not execution success.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Every selected FortiGate installed the latest revision
choices.feedback: Installation must be checked in Task Monitor and per-device results.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The next run passed syntax verification on all devices
choices.feedback: A schedule can exist before the next run and before any device verification occurs.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The package has no pending configuration differences
choices.feedback: Pending differences are separate from the existence of a schedule.

questions.stem: One device fails verification during a scheduled package install. What is the best next step?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delete the schedule and repeat the same install
choices.feedback: Repeating the same task without correcting the device-specific cause will reproduce the failure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Inspect that device's verification report and unsupported command
choices.feedback: Correct: inspect the per-device verification output and identify the model or firmware command mismatch.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Assume the package failed on every selected device
choices.feedback: FortiManager creates per-device results; one failure does not prove every target failed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Increase the schedule recurrence until installation succeeds
choices.feedback: Changing recurrence does not correct syntax or model compatibility.

questions.stem: Which fields define the recurring policy-package installation schedule?

choices.label: A
choices.text: ADOM name, device serial, policy checksum and retries
choices.feedback: Those fields do not define the documented recurrence schedule.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Package name, revision number, user role and timeout
choices.feedback: Package identity and user role matter elsewhere, but they are not the recurrence definition.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Start date/time, recurrence pattern, targets and end date
choices.feedback: Correct: recurrence uses a start time, daily/weekly/monthly pattern, target devices and an end condition.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Firmware version, interface address, tunnel name and SLA
choices.feedback: These are device or SD-WAN attributes, not schedule fields.

questions.stem: An operator edits a package after a recurring schedule is created. What should happen before its next run?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assume the old preview remains valid indefinitely
choices.feedback: The preview can become stale when package content changes.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Duplicate the schedule to capture the package change
choices.feedback: Duplicating the schedule risks overlapping installs and does not validate the changed package.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Move every target device into another ADOM
choices.feedback: Moving devices between ADOMs is unrelated and may create additional scope problems.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reopen the package and verify the current install preview
choices.feedback: Correct: verify the current package and target set before the scheduled execution.

questions.stem: AI Access Visibility is empty immediately after an upgrade. What should be checked first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Source authorization, log forwarding and required FortiGate log families
choices.feedback: Correct: the dashboard depends on authorized source devices and DLP, DNS, Web Filter and Application Control logs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Only the dashboard theme and browser cache
choices.feedback: Browser rendering cannot explain a missing source event pipeline.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only the FortiAnalyzer report schedule and output format
choices.feedback: Report scheduling is separate from the AI Access Visibility log aggregation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The user's password and the ADOM display name
choices.feedback: User authentication and ADOM naming do not prove that source logs are arriving.

questions.stem: The Categories widget labels an AI application as sanctioned. Where does that label originate?

choices.label: A
choices.text: FortiAnalyzer infers it from user browsing duration
choices.feedback: Browsing duration is not the documented source of the sanctioned attribute.

choices.label: B
choices.text: FortiGate configuration supplies the sanctioned classification
choices.feedback: Correct: the sanctioned/unsanctioned label is supplied through FortiGate configuration or metadata.

choices.label: C
choices.text: FortiGuard automatically approves every application in that category
choices.feedback: Category classification and sanctioned status are different concepts.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The user identity provider writes the dashboard label
choices.feedback: Identity providers do not author this FortiGate application classification.

questions.stem: Application activity appears, but the DLP threat widget remains empty. What is the best check?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rebuild the ADOM database before checking policies
choices.feedback: Rebuilding the database is disproportionate before validating source DLP logs.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change the dashboard refresh interval to one minute
choices.feedback: Refresh frequency changes display timing, not the existence of DLP events.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Verify DLP sensor coverage and event logging on FortiGate
choices.feedback: Correct: DLP requires an applied sensor and logging of the relevant actions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable Application Control to force DLP events
choices.feedback: Application Control is a separate log source and disabling it does not create DLP events.

questions.stem: Collector forwarding is disconnected and server-auth state remains Query after upgrade. What is indicated?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The AI category taxonomy is missing a sanctioned label
choices.feedback: AI category taxonomy does not control the Collector's transport authentication state.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The dashboard has reached its maximum widget count
choices.feedback: Widget count does not affect Collector-to-Analyzer authentication.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The DLP sensor is matching too many documents
choices.feedback: DLP match volume does not explain a disconnected forwarding channel.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The source transport or certificate identity check is failing
choices.feedback: Correct: inspect the Collector certificate common name, trust and forwarding connection before troubleshooting dashboard widgets.

questions.stem: FortiSwitchOS automatic system-time mode selects sources in which order?

choices.label: A
choices.text: PTP, then NTP, then manual local time
choices.feedback: Correct: automatic mode prefers PTP, falls back to NTP, then uses manual local time.

choices.label: B
choices.text: NTP, then manual local time, then PTP
choices.feedback: NTP is second, not first, when a valid PTP source exists.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Manual local time, then PTP, then NTP
choices.feedback: Manual time is the last fallback, not the preferred source.

choices.label: D
choices.text: PTP, then manual local time, then NTP
choices.feedback: Manual time follows NTP, not PTP.

questions.stem: An NTP server responds, but the switch still uses another clock source. What proves selection?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The NTP server's DNS record and ping response
choices.feedback: Reachability shows the server can be contacted, not that automatic arbitration selected it.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The saved NTP configuration in the GUI only
choices.feedback: Correct: inspect live synchronization status and the selected source, not only saved configuration.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The configured NTP polling interval value
choices.feedback: A polling interval does not identify which source currently disciplines the clock.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Diagnose sys ntp status and the selected source
choices.feedback: A GUI configuration screenshot does not prove current source selection.

questions.stem: SNMPv3 reports USM not in time window while credentials are correct. What is most likely?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The SNMP view excludes the requested interface
choices.feedback: An SNMP view controls accessible objects, not the USM time-window check.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The switch has no DNS record for its hostname
choices.feedback: DNS may affect name resolution but does not explain a time-window rejection after packets reach the agent.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The switch and manager clocks have excessive skew
choices.feedback: Correct: compare engine time, stratum and clock offset on both systems.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The community string has the wrong capitalization
choices.feedback: SNMPv3 uses user security parameters, not the SNMPv2c community string.

questions.stem: PTP becomes invalid while an NTP candidate remains valid in automatic mode. What should occur?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The switch stays on PTP until reboot
choices.feedback: Automatic selection is intended to use the highest-priority valid source, not pin an invalid PTP source.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The switch disables all time-dependent services
choices.feedback: Loss of PTP does not require disabling SNMP, logs or scheduled services.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The switch switches directly to manual local time
choices.feedback: Manual local time is the last fallback when NTP is also unavailable.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The selector falls back to the valid NTP source
choices.feedback: Correct: NTP is the next valid source after PTP.

questions.stem: A maintenance window must stop every SSID on radio 2 but preserve configuration. Which setting fits?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Delete each VAP from the shared WTP profile
choices.feedback: Deleting VAPs destroys the retained configuration the maintenance task is trying to preserve.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set vap-status disable under the radio profile
choices.feedback: Correct: vap-status suppresses all configured VAP broadcasts on that radio while retaining assignments.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Remove the SSID objects from the WLAN database
choices.feedback: Deleting SSID objects makes restoration a reconstruction task.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable the CAPWAP tunnel for the affected APs
choices.feedback: CAPWAP shutdown removes controller connectivity rather than only stopping radio VAP broadcasts.

questions.stem: One AP keeps advertising an SSID after the shared profile disables radio 2. What should be inspected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The RADIUS server's accounting-stop timer
choices.feedback: Accounting timers do not determine radio broadcast state.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The AP's per-device override-vap-status setting
choices.feedback: Correct: a per-device override can take precedence over the shared WTP profile.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer ADOM's log retention setting
choices.feedback: Log retention has no effect on whether an AP advertises a VAP.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The DHCP server's lease-time configuration
choices.feedback: DHCP lease time affects client addressing after association, not beacon transmission.

questions.stem: The SSID beacon disappears, but the AP remains connected to the controller. What does this suggest?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The AP has lost PoE and powered down
choices.feedback: A powered-down AP cannot remain connected to the controller.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The CAPWAP tunnel has been deleted
choices.feedback: A deleted CAPWAP tunnel would remove controller connectivity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The radio's VAP broadcast state is disabled
choices.feedback: Correct: VAP broadcast can be disabled while SSID objects and CAPWAP control remain present.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The SSID security profile has been removed
choices.feedback: A removed security profile is not required to stop beacon advertisement.

questions.stem: APs repeatedly leave and rejoin with DTLS peer-disconnected messages. What is the right focus?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Recreate every SSID before checking connectivity
choices.feedback: SSID recreation does not repair a CAPWAP control-path failure.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Change the radio's VAP status to enabled
choices.feedback: VAP status controls WLAN advertisement, not DTLS peer liveness.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the DHCP lease time for wireless clients
choices.feedback: DHCP lease duration is unrelated to CAPWAP keepalive loss.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Inspect CAPWAP keepalives, DTLS and uplink captures
choices.feedback: Correct: investigate the AP/controller transport path and missed keepalive responses.

questions.stem: A newly connected endpoint should be visible by device type. Which widget answers that?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Recent Hosts
choices.feedback: Correct: Recent Hosts shows newly discovered hosts grouped by type.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Top Host Activity
choices.feedback: Top Host Activity ranks connection activity, not newly discovered device types.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Logical Network Access
choices.feedback: Logical Network Access shows hosts associated with a logical network during a period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: RADIUS
choices.feedback: RADIUS shows authentication success/failure events.

questions.stem: One endpoint generates unusually frequent connections during the last hour. Which widget is most useful?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Recent Hosts
choices.feedback: Recent Hosts answers discovery timing, not connection-volume ranking.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Top Host Activity
choices.feedback: Correct: Top Host Activity ranks hosts by connection activity over the selected period.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Logical Network Access
choices.feedback: Logical Network Access shows host-to-network association, not activity ranking.

choices.label: D
choices.text: RADIUS
choices.feedback: RADIUS summarizes authentication outcomes, not general connection activity.

questions.stem: An auditor asks which hosts accessed a specific logical network yesterday. Which view fits?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Recent Hosts
choices.feedback: Recent Hosts is about newly discovered endpoints.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Top Host Activity
choices.feedback: Top Host Activity ranks connection events, not membership in a logical network.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Logical Network Access
choices.feedback: Correct: Logical Network Access lists hosts associated with each logical network over a chosen period.

choices.label: D
choices.text: RADIUS
choices.feedback: RADIUS counts authentication outcomes and does not directly answer logical-network access.

questions.stem: RADIUS successes are high, but endpoints still land in the wrong logical network. What next?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Assume Access-Accept proves the VLAN was applied
choices.feedback: Access-Accept proves authentication acceptance, not successful VLAN/role application.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Clear all Recent Hosts entries and retry
choices.feedback: Clearing discovery data removes evidence and does not fix mapping.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Increase the Top Host Activity time window
choices.feedback: Activity window changes do not correct authorization attributes.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Correlate RADIUS attributes with host and network-device state
choices.feedback: Correct: inspect returned role/VLAN attributes and verify the network device applied them.

questions.stem: The goal is to cap simultaneous authenticated endpoint sessions. Which counter should be selected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Registered Host
choices.feedback: Registered Host limits how many endpoints are registered, not necessarily active now.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Logged in Host
choices.feedback: Logged in Host is the right counter, so this choice would measure active sessions instead of registered devices.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Recent Host
choices.feedback: Recent Host is a discovery widget, not a FortiNAC-F concurrent-session counter.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Top Host Activity
choices.feedback: Top Host Activity is a dashboard metric, not a session-limit type.

questions.stem: A user has a global limit of two but an individual limit of four. Which applies?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The lower value always wins across all scopes
choices.feedback: FortiNAC-F documents individual-user precedence rather than a minimum-value rule.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The individual user's limit overrides the global limit
choices.feedback: Correct: the per-user value overrides the global value for that user.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The global limit overrides every user setting
choices.feedback: Global settings apply when no individual override takes precedence.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The two values are added to create six sessions
choices.feedback: Limits are not additive.

questions.stem: An administrator wants a separate concurrent-session cap for a user group. What is supported?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Create a group policy under Allowed Hosts
choices.feedback: FortiNAC-F does not expose the feature at user-group scope.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Set the group cap in RADIUS accounting
choices.feedback: RADIUS accounting supplies session evidence, not a FortiNAC group limit object.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Use per-user overrides because group-level limits are unavailable
choices.feedback: Correct: configure a global default and individual-user overrides; no group-level setting is available.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Set the limit on every access switch port
choices.feedback: Port-level limits do not implement the documented FortiNAC-F user-session policy.

questions.stem: FortiNAC sends Disconnect-Request, but the NAS returns Disconnect-NAK. What does that prove?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The user session has ended successfully
choices.feedback: A successful session end would require an accepted disconnect or subsequent stop evidence.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The accounting stop was received and stored
choices.feedback: Disconnect-NAK is not an Accounting-Stop message.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The host was deleted from FortiNAC
choices.feedback: Host deletion is not implied by a rejected request.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The NAS rejected the disconnect request
choices.feedback: Correct: inspect missing session-identifying attributes and confirm the NAS later ends the session.

questions.stem: An RSA certificate is rejected after the SHA-1 removal notice. What must be inspected first?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The certificate's signature digest algorithm
choices.feedback: Correct: SHA-1 can be the certificate signature digest even when the public key is RSA.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The RSA public-key length alone
choices.feedback: Key length does not identify the digest used to sign the certificate.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The certificate's friendly name only
choices.feedback: A friendly name is a local label, not a cryptographic property.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The subject's organizational unit field
choices.feedback: The organizational unit is subject metadata, not the signature algorithm.

questions.stem: A certificate chain uses SHA-1 signing. What is the preferred migration?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Increase RSA key size but keep SHA-1
choices.feedback: A larger RSA key does not remove SHA-1 from the certificate signature.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Reissue certificates with SHA-256 or stronger
choices.feedback: Correct: reissue affected certificates and chains using a supported SHA-2-or-stronger digest.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Change the certificate subject without reissuing
choices.feedback: Changing the subject field does not change the signature digest.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Disable certificate validation on relying systems
choices.feedback: Disabling validation weakens authentication rather than fixing the chain.

questions.stem: A Mobility Agent reports NT_STATUS_MORE_PROCESSING_REQUIRED after a Windows update. What should not be assumed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: That the certificate signature uses SHA-1
choices.feedback: Correct: NTLM signing/negotiation is separate from X.509 SHA-1 certificate-signature processing.

choices.label: B
choices.text: That the agent reached the domain controller
choices.feedback: Reachability may be relevant, but it is not the only possible cause.

choices.label: C
choices.text: That the error belongs to NTLM negotiation
choices.feedback: The error is associated with the NTLM exchange and should be investigated at that layer.

choices.label: D
choices.text: That the FAC version is relevant
choices.feedback: FAC and agent compatibility can matter for this separate authentication workflow.

questions.stem: An integration cannot yet move off SHA-1 before upgrade. What is the documented fallback?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disable all certificate authentication permanently
choices.feedback: Disabling all certificate authentication is not the documented fallback and may break unrelated services.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Replace the FAC appliance with a RADIUS proxy
choices.feedback: A RADIUS proxy does not restore SHA-1 signing support on FAC.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ignore the warning and upgrade without testing
choices.feedback: Ignoring the notice risks breaking dependent cryptographic operations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Use the vendor-documented 6.5.3 compatibility fallback
choices.feedback: Correct: Fortinet documents 6.5.3 as the fallback if SHA-1 support is indispensable; migration remains preferable.

questions.stem: An auto-provisioned user has been inactive past the first threshold. What happens?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The user is disabled and a User Event is logged
choices.feedback: Correct: the inactivity stage disables the auto-provisioned account and records a system event.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The user is immediately deleted from the database
choices.feedback: Deletion is the second stage after the disabled-retention timer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The user is converted into a manual local account
choices.feedback: The feature does not convert account provisioning type.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The user's secrets are automatically transferred to admin
choices.feedback: The documentation does not promise automatic secret ownership transfer.

questions.stem: A disabled auto-provisioned user remains for another retention period. Which setting controls deletion?

choices.label: A
choices.text: User Max Inactivity Days
choices.feedback: User Max Inactivity Days controls the first disable stage, not purge after disable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: User Max Disabled Days
choices.feedback: Correct: User Max Disabled Days defines how long a disabled provisioned user remains before deletion.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Password Expiry Warning Days
choices.feedback: Password warning settings do not control user-account lifecycle.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Session Recording Retention Days
choices.feedback: Session recording retention is separate from user cleanup.

questions.stem: An organization sets User Max Disabled Days to zero. What is the effect?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Disabled users are purged immediately
choices.feedback: Zero does not mean immediate deletion; it disables that stage.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All manual users are disabled after one day
choices.feedback: Manual users are outside this auto-provisioned cleanup policy.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The automatic deletion stage is disabled
choices.feedback: Correct: a value of zero disables automatic purge of disabled users.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The inactivity timer changes to zero hours
choices.feedback: The setting is a day-count threshold, not a time-of-day conversion.

questions.stem: A manually created local user remains after the purge threshold. Is that expected?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No, every user type shares the same purge policy
choices.feedback: The feature is not a universal deletion policy for every user.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No, the user must first be disabled by RADIUS
choices.feedback: RADIUS disablement is not the criterion for this lifecycle feature.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Only users with secrets are exempt from purge
choices.feedback: Secret ownership is not the documented scope selector.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Yes, the cleanup applies to auto-provisioned users
choices.feedback: Correct: verify the account's provisioning source; manual users are not the auto-provisioned cleanup target.

questions.stem: An Event Log Integrity row reports Success. What does that prove?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The stored checksum matches the recalculated checksum
choices.feedback: Correct: Success indicates the checksum comparison matched for that partition.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The original event source was truthful and complete
choices.feedback: Checksum integrity does not validate the truth of the source event.

choices.label: C
choices.text: No event was deleted before archive creation
choices.feedback: The feature cannot prove that no event was deleted before the archive existed.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The entire ClickHouse cluster has a current backup
choices.feedback: Event integrity is not a backup-status report.

questions.stem: The Event Integrity view reports Not Found for a partition. What is the right interpretation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The checksum matched and validation succeeded
choices.feedback: Success is the status for a matching checksum.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The partition is missing or detached
choices.feedback: Correct: Not Found indicates the event partition/log file is absent or detached.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The validator encountered a shell parsing error
choices.feedback: System Error represents a validator execution or parsing problem.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The event has not yet been validated
choices.feedback: Not Validated is the status for a check that has not run.

questions.stem: Why is automatic Event Log Integrity validation off by default?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It is supported only on Elasticsearch
choices.feedback: Fortinet documents the feature for ClickHouse, not Elasticsearch.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It prevents manual validation from running
choices.feedback: Manual validation remains available independently of automatic validation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is resource-intensive during ClickHouse consolidation
choices.feedback: Correct: automatic checks run at consolidation and consume resources.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It deletes the checksum after each validation
choices.feedback: The checksum is used for comparison; it is not simply deleted after validation.

questions.stem: Partition name and validation status are blank for a ClickHouse event row. What should be checked?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Whether the user has a valid MFA token
choices.feedback: MFA does not explain a missing ClickHouse partition name.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Whether the firewall policy permits DNS
choices.feedback: Firewall DNS policy is unrelated to the database consolidation state.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Whether the event rule has a severity value
choices.feedback: Event severity does not determine partition consolidation.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whether storage pressure prevented ClickHouse consolidation
choices.feedback: Correct: insufficient storage can prevent consolidation and leave those fields blank.

questions.stem: A FortiExtender management address overlaps a customer LAN. Which setting is relevant?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The FortiExtender/LAN Extension control-plane subnet
choices.feedback: Correct: the dedicated control-plane subnet allocates management addresses to FortiExtender/LAN Extension.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The remote-agent IPAM pool for VPN clients
choices.feedback: Remote-agent IPAM is a separate pool and does not solve this control-plane collision.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The browser isolation profile for web access
choices.feedback: Browser isolation has no effect on FortiExtender management addressing.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The endpoint posture tag for device compliance
choices.feedback: Posture tags do not allocate control-plane addresses.

questions.stem: A custom control-plane subnet reverts after a BGP configuration save. What is documented?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The IPAM pool is automatically merged with BGP
choices.feedback: IPAM is a separate address-management feature.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The BGP save resets the control-plane subnet to default
choices.feedback: Correct: Fortinet documents a caveat where saving BGP restores the default control-plane subnet.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The FortiExtender retains the old address indefinitely
choices.feedback: Do not assume the old custom subnet remains active after the save.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The custom subnet is moved into the agent pool
choices.feedback: The feature does not move the control-plane range into the remote-agent pool.

questions.stem: After a custom control-plane subnet is applied, what happens to the old 10.253.0.0/16 reservation?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It becomes the new default control-plane subnet
choices.feedback: The default control-plane subnet remains 10.252.0.0/16.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It remains reserved for every FortiExtender
choices.feedback: Fortinet documents that the old reservation is removed after customization.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is removed from the previous reserved set
choices.feedback: Correct: the former 10.253.0.0/16 reservation is removed when a custom control-plane subnet is configured.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It becomes the remote-agent pool automatically
choices.feedback: The remote-agent pool is configured separately and is not automatically replaced.

questions.stem: A remote agent needs a different address pool. Which area should be changed?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The FortiExtender control-plane subnet under Advanced
choices.feedback: The control-plane subnet is for FortiExtender/LAN Extension management addresses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The BGP router ID on the SPA tunnel
choices.feedback: BGP router IDs identify routing speakers; they do not allocate remote-agent addresses.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The LAN Extension management subnet only
choices.feedback: LAN Extension management addressing is not the remote-agent IPAM pool.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The remote-agent IPAM pool and exclusions
choices.feedback: Correct: remote-agent and edge-endpoint pools are managed separately under IPAM.

questions.stem: FortiOS 8.0 removes the old speed-test retry parameters. What replaces their behavior?

choices.label: A
choices.text: FortiGate/backend coordination handles retries
choices.feedback: Correct: the new coordination mechanism manages retry behavior between FortiGate and the backend.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The interface shaper retries each failed test
choices.feedback: Interface shaping controls traffic rates, not the test retry scheduler.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The administrator must configure a retry cron job
choices.feedback: A separate cron job is not the documented replacement.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The speed-test server disables all retries
choices.feedback: The server does not simply disable all retries.

questions.stem: A speed test completes, but production shaping still uses the manual value. What is missing?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The test schedule needs another weekly occurrence
choices.feedback: Another schedule does not change which bandwidth source the interface uses.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The interface bandwidth source must select measured
choices.feedback: Correct: measured values must be selected by inbandwidth-source/outbandwidth-source.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The tunnel must switch from IPsec to GRE
choices.feedback: Changing tunnel encapsulation is not required for measured bandwidth selection.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The test server needs a larger TCP window
choices.feedback: TCP window tuning does not select the measured interface bandwidth.

questions.stem: A minimum value of 20,000 is intended as kbps. What must be verified?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The BGP local preference on the WAN member
choices.feedback: BGP local preference does not define speed-test min/max units.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The policy package's ADOM revision number
choices.feedback: ADOM revision numbers are unrelated to the speed-test value interpretation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The speed-test bandwidth-limit unit
choices.feedback: Correct: the default unit is kbps, but the configured unit can be percentage.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The FortiAnalyzer ADOM timezone
choices.feedback: ADOM time zone does not change bandwidth-unit semantics.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly describes speed-test traffic in FortiOS 8.0?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It always uses the ordinary interface shaper
choices.feedback: The speed-test traffic does not use the ordinary interface shaper.

choices.label: B
choices.text: It bypasses every configured bandwidth limit
choices.feedback: It still observes speed-test-specific minimum and maximum settings.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is shaped only by the VPN traffic class
choices.feedback: VPN traffic classes are not the only control point.

choices.label: D
choices.text: It bypasses normal shaping but respects test caps
choices.feedback: Correct: test traffic bypasses ordinary shaping but remains bounded by speed-test min/max controls.

questions.stem: A VPN speed test reports throughput. Which command helps prove shaping consumed it?

choices.label: A
choices.text: diagnose vpn tunnel list and inspect egress traffic control bandwidth
choices.feedback: Correct: tunnel output exposes the egress traffic-control bandwidth applied to the overlay.

choices.label: B
choices.text: diagnose debug application ike and inspect proposal selection
choices.feedback: IKE proposal output proves negotiation, not the shaping value.

choices.label: C
choices.text: diagnose sys ntp status and inspect selected time source
choices.feedback: NTP status is unrelated to speed-test shaping.

choices.label: D
choices.text: diagnose firewall iprope list and inspect policy order
choices.feedback: Policy order does not show measured bandwidth selection.

questions.stem: An operator runs a manual speed test. Does that automatically change shaping?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, every test forces both bandwidth sources to measured
choices.feedback: The interface does not automatically switch its bandwidth source after every test.

choices.label: B
choices.text: No, interface source selection still controls effective shaping
choices.feedback: Correct: a test can update measured fields, but source selection determines whether shaping uses them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Yes, but only when BGP is disabled on the tunnel
choices.feedback: BGP state is not the condition for measured source selection.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No, because manual tests never update measured fields
choices.feedback: Manual tests can update measured fields; they simply do not guarantee shaping uses them.
